blocking_findings.body: The declaration the human approval will bind lists 'exact-head CI success for that head' as a precondition of GO, and at the readiness head that precondition is not pending but failed: FULL_NATIVE run 35509978669 fails the MLX small-fixture job at generate_f017_v11_measurement_v1.py --check because scripts/research/f017_corrected_oracle_primary_wrapper_v11.py drifted from the measurement-v8 binding (f35d3411) at commit 5b39a21a. Recording a GO against a declaration whose own stated precondition is known-failed is a governance contradiction regardless of whether the failing check touches the native executor. The addendum's argument that the drift is pre-existing and planner-owned may be correct, but that scoping decision has to live in the bound declaration, not in a review packet. The drifted file is also the corrected oracle's primary wrapper, i.e. the lineage of the expected token 154820 itself, so an unreconciled binding there cannot be waved through silently.
blocking_findings.evidence: Declaration v2 remaining_before_go[1] 'exact-head CI success for that head'; cycle-02 addendum: 'fails: working tree differs from measurement head: scripts/research/f017_corrected_oracle_primary_wrapper_v11.py ... no FULL_NATIVE run has passed on the branch since'.
blocking_findings.remedy: Either (a) re-bind the V11 measurement to the accepted Event 06 path so FULL_NATIVE passes at a new head, or (b) issue declaration v3 (new file, append-only) that replaces the CI precondition with an explicit, narrowed gate (classification + Apple Silicon workspace baseline SUCCESS at the exact head) and records the measurement-check failure, its cause (5b39a21a vs f35d3411), and why it is independent of the executor, contract validation and the differentials. In both cases the readiness head changes; re-run validate-contract and machine preflight there and submit a cycle-03 packet.

blocking_findings.body: The material this review was told to review verbatim is not the material at the readiness head. After the cycle-01 packet was assembled, Cargo.toml changed (30ca81dc), contract v3 was re-bound to a new sha (7f984043..., given only as an 8-hex-character prefix), and 'declaration v2 and template carry the new contract sha', meaning a versioned declaration was mutated in place. The inline declaration v2 still shows contract sha 389580fa..., the inline contract shows the pre-30ca81dc Cargo.toml sha, and the inline diff shows a Cargo.toml that no longer matches the head. A banked 'final independent review with exact request/response' bound to a declaration and contract the reviewer never saw verbatim, with a truncated sha, does not close the binding chain the approval schema relies on.
blocking_findings.evidence: Cycle-02 addendum: 'd690a967 (contract v3 code-manifest re-bound after the Cargo.toml change; declaration v2 and template carry the new contract sha)'; 'Contract v3 sha256 7f984043...'; inline DOMAIN DECLARATION v2 admission_contract.sha256 = 389580fa7ba5ca0f8a8d531aa522431bae9b47db413a02fba69b15e2132356f4; inline SOURCE DIFF Cargo.toml declares f017-native-synthetic-differential, which 30ca81dc restored to the auto-discovered name.
blocking_findings.remedy: Cycle-03 packet must inline, verbatim, the declaration (as a new version, not an in-place edit of v2), the admission contract v3 as committed at the readiness head, the corrected-oracle binding, and the full 64-hex sha256 of each; the readiness head must be the commit that contains exactly those files; the review response is then bound to those shas.

non_blocking_required_findings.body: The GO record must be an informed one. Nothing in the packet states what, if anything, changed in the native numerics path (loader, model, executor, quant, stream, MLX bridge) between the attempt-1 executor and f017-native-bounded-p1-v2; the visible source diff c23e58ec..50a66db0 touches only contract.rs and new differential bins. If the numerics are unchanged, the run is deterministic (greedy, empty KV, single-threaded env) and the most probable outcome is observed 17351 again, i.e. a banked terminal failure whose real payoff is the evidenced-v4 forward evidence, not a success. The human must also be told that the one-shot authority is consumed at durable start (a crash or jetsam after that point spends the attempt), and what a failure at 154820 permanently prohibits afterwards.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: H01 ledger: attempt 1 observed 17351 vs frozen 21615; corrected oracle 154820; reconciliation conclusion: the divergence 'is NOT explained by decoder or graph defects reproducible without the checkpoint'; declaration one_shot.expected_duration 'after durable start'; binding attempt_1.disposition 'retry PERMANENTLY_PROHIBITED'.
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: Add to the readiness note (and the approval body) a short statement of the executor numerical delta since attempt 1 (or 'none'), the resulting prior expectation, the durable-start consumption rule, and the post-failure prohibition scope; the human's plain-words GO should be re-confirmed against that statement.

non_blocking_required_findings.body: The stream crate still exports EXPECTED_TOKEN (21615); the packet asserts the executor binds the authority's expected_token at execute-evidenced-v4, but no inline material shows that the receipt's success/failure classification and the mandatory-stop verdict use the authority/contract token rather than stream::EXPECTED_TOKEN, nor that the executor cross-checks authority.expected_token == contract.one_shot.expected_token == 154820 and authority.attempt_id == contract.one_shot.attempt_id. The negative controls exercise validate_static only, not execution-time classification.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: contract.rs test 'assert_ne!(CORRECTED_EXPECTED_TOKEN, stream::EXPECTED_TOKEN)'; binding note 'the executor binds the authority's expected_token (154820) at execute-evidenced-v4'; STATIC VALIDATION NEGATIVE CONTROLS cover contract fields only.
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: By inspection (no code change), enumerate every use of stream::EXPECTED_TOKEN and every comparison producing the receipt verdict in bounded_p1.rs / p1_domain.rs / executor.rs, confirm the verdict and stop logic use the authority-bound token and that the authority/contract cross-check exists, and record the finding with file:line in the readiness note. If any path uses 21615 or the cross-check is absent, that is a code change and a new head/review.

non_blocking_required_findings.body: The provenance of 154820 relative to the wrapper drift is unstated: the packet gives Event 06 sequence 43 immutable_execution_source c3526d68 and implementation 4b48167f, but not whether those include 5b39a21a's change to f017_corrected_oracle_primary_wrapper_v11.py, nor whether f017_corrected_oracle_primary_numerics_v3._execute_graph used by the N3 graph differential is byte-identical to the module that produced the Event 06 payloads.
non_blocking_required_findings.evidence: Corrected-oracle binding source {c3526d68, 4b48167f}; addendum 'commit 5b39a21a (2026-09-03 ...) changed it'; reconciliation n3_graph_differential.oracle 'f017_corrected_oracle_primary_numerics_v3.py _execute_graph'.
non_blocking_required_findings.remedy: Record in the readiness note: the ancestry relation of c3526d68/4b48167f to 5b39a21a, that the wrapper change is gate-path only (or otherwise), and the sha256 of f017_corrected_oracle_primary_numerics_v3.py at Event 06 vs at the readiness head.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: execution_code_head (5e32d68f, the executor's build source) and the code_manifest tree (re-bound at d690a967 after the Cargo.toml change) now differ; the difference is bin declarations only, but the executor-sha-to-manifest link is no longer exact by construction.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: Addendum: 'contract v3 code-manifest re-bound after the Cargo.toml change ... executor unchanged'; contract execution_code_head 5e32d68f.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Rebuild f017-native-bounded-p1 in release on the M1 Ultra at the readiness head with the pinned keg and compare to 91e50a0b...; if identical, record it; if not, rebind. Document execution_code_head semantics as 'build-source head' distinct from the manifest tree.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Branch/head race: the approval commit will move HEAD past the readiness head, pushing it will re-trigger the failing FULL_NATIVE run, and the work branch remains a fast-forward source. Nothing inline shows the authorize step pins HEAD to 'approval commit whose parent is the readiness head'.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: Declaration prepared_on_branch; remaining_before_go[3] 'then ... authorize mints the one-shot authority'.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Have the authorize step assert HEAD == approval commit, HEAD^ == readiness head, clean tree, equal to origin/feat/017-rust-native-inference-runtime; do not touch the branch between approval push and execution regardless of CI status.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: 'Pause' of the legacy resident service is ambiguous; a SIGSTOP'd process keeps its memory and any Metal/unified-memory allocations resident, which the vm_stat gate would reflect but which still competes with the native run.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: Declaration one_shot.memory; addendum 'legacy resident service idle and will be paused before execution'.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Quit the service rather than stopping it, take the vm_stat sample within 5 s of admission, run under caffeinate, and record the sample.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Contract binds six shard sha256s but the ~2-3 minute duration and 0 checkpoint reads at plan-only imply shard hashes are not recomputed at execution; the hard-linked directory's integrity therefore rests on a prior census.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: Contract checkpoint.shards; declaration plan_only '0 checkpoint reads'; expected_duration '~2-3 minutes'.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: State whether execute-evidenced-v4 verifies shard sha256s; if not, record the last full hash census of the hard-linked directory and stat (inode, size, mtime) immediately before execution.

defense_in_depth_findings.body: Reviewer provenance: this reviewer was spawned as a subagent by the preparing session after the headless CLI was found not logged in, and read the packet through a single file-read tool call rather than 'no tools'.
defense_in_depth_findings.evidence: Addendum 'Reviewer availability' paragraph; this review's own conduct.
defense_in_depth_findings.remedy: Bank the exact spawn prompt, the packet path and its sha256, and this response verbatim; note the single-file-read deviation from 'no tools' in the banked record.

rationale: No blocking technical defect was found in the inline substance: generation-3 validation adds a closed schema map, keeps the generation-2 tuple (attempt 1, 21615, v2 receipt) intact, requires a sha-bound corrected-oracle document whose token, attempt id, mode and both selected tokens are checked against a compiled constant, and every negative control is rejected; the corrected token 154820 is well supported (primary/secondary agree, 3.53 top-1 margin, pinned payload hashes, public evidence commit) and attempt 2 is a legitimately new question, not a disguised retry; the checkpoint-free reconciliation removes cheap explanations for attempt 1 but proves nothing about real geometry, loader byte ranges (by inspection only) or MLX kernels at scale. The REJECT is on governance completeness, not on the executor: the declaration to be bound states a CI-success precondition that is failed at the readiness head, and the artifacts at that head (contract v3, declaration, Cargo.toml) differ from what this review was given verbatim, with the new contract sha truncated. Both are fixable in one further cycle at a new head; with B-01 and B-02 closed and R-01..R-03 satisfied, an ACCEPT_FOR_SINGLE_BOUNDED_M1_ULTRA_P1 verdict would be reachable. The human's already-expressed GO was not treated as evidence.
